answer: The haven test I would run is DNS resolver history consistency: the same resolvers used from the same home network, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. A farm that reuses one proof across ten accounts is caught at the second account, because the same resolvers used from the same home network is bound to a single identity — the tundra is that reuse itself becomes the evidence. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the crystal of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out.
